answers.rationale: American is the best balance here: it is a nonstop, costs $22 less than Delta, arrives only 15 minutes later on Tuesday when afternoon arrival is acceptable, and gives 25 more minutes of Thursday buffer after the 11:30 session. It also retains the user's preferred standard window option. Maya treats Delta as a tie-breaker when price and schedule are otherwise close, not as a reason to accept an inferior schedule/value combination.
unsupported_assumptions: The 2:40 p.m. DCA departure leaves adequate airport-transfer and security time after the 11:30 a.m. session.
There is no unstated Delta-only corporate, status, or loyalty benefit.

answers.rationale: Delta A is a nonstop that gets Maya to MSY with a very large margin before the 5:30 p.m. prep call, preserves a no-fee window seat, and returns comfortably after a late-morning closeout. The $7 saving and modestly later return on Southwest do not outweigh the loss of assigned seating/window control for a work itinerary when the schedules otherwise both work.
unsupported_assumptions: Normal airport-to-hotel transfer and check-in timing will allow the noon arrival to reach the hotel well before the prep call.
There is no material business requirement for the extra 40 minutes offered by Southwest's return.

answers.rationale: The 2:05 p.m. flight is inconsistent with a sign-off scheduled through 12:45 p.m., possible Q&A, and a 25-minute trip to MKE, even with carry-on only. The 5:35 p.m. Delta nonstop gives a real cushion at the same fare class. The one-stop is later and less resilient, while the 7:15 p.m. nonstop buys only $8 of savings at a substantially later arrival.
unsupported_assumptions: There is no separate need to be back in Atlanta before the 8:40 p.m. arrival on the 5:35 p.m. nonstop.

answers.rationale: The undecided closing huddle makes both the 2:20 p.m. and 3:05 p.m. options dependent on an on-time, short finish and a quick airport transfer. Maya repeatedly chooses a later nonstop for a modest premium when the client end time is uncertain, rather than making a client departure rushed. The 5:05 p.m. Delta nonstop supplies the needed buffer and avoids both Southwest open seating and the much later one-stop itinerary.
unsupported_assumptions: No client clarification can be obtained before ticketing that would reliably rule out the closing huddle.
A later Atlanta arrival is acceptable for this trip.
